subject.title: feat(setup): offer native Windows and WSL gateway modes

question: Should native Windows gateway mode ship as a clearly lower-isolation alternative while WSL 2 remains the recommended setup?
rationale: Code review can repair gateway supervision and assess ownership mechanics, but maintainers must decide whether direct Windows user-context gateway execution is an acceptable product security boundary.

options.title: Ship after recovery fix
options.body: Keep WSL 2 recommended, repair unexpected native exit recovery, retain the lower-isolation disclosure, and require exact-head upgrade and lifecycle proof.

options.title: Gate as experimental
options.body: Expose native Windows only through an advanced or experimental affordance while more containment and reliability evidence is gathered.

options.title: Defer native mode
options.body: Pause the feature until maintainers want to support the additional security and operational boundary.

recommendation.title: Ship after recovery fix
recommendation.body: Keep WSL 2 recommended, repair unexpected native exit recovery, retain the lower-isolation disclosure, and require exact-head upgrade and lifecycle proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They performed the detailed safety and parity review and authored the current product framing and lifecycle corrections.
